provenance.author: Vincent Russo
provenance.method: by hand: CS = ((1+i)/2) I + ((1-i)/2) CZ applied to |++>, coefficients fitted exactly by fit_coeffs.fit

compute.hardware: Apple silicon laptop, one core; direct construction, no search

notes: |CS> = CS|++> = (|00> + |01> + |10> + i|11>)/2 is the magic state of the two-qubit controlled-S gate, the first width-2 orbit on the board: m copies live on 2m qubits and gamma = log_2(rank)/m is still per copy. CS = ((1+i)/2) I + ((1-i)/2) CZ, so |CS> = ((1+i)/2)|++> + ((1-i)/2) CZ|++>, two stabilizer terms with coefficients in Q(i); the identity is checked symbolically by the verifier. With the exact rank-1 exclusion of cert_cs_m2_rank2.py this settles chi(|CS>) = 2. No exponent has been published for the CS orbit, so under the board's convention its baseline is the single-copy product bound log_2 chi(|CS>) = 1, labeled as such on every page. Comparison lines from the literature: the extent exponent log_2(8/5) = 0.678 (F(CS) = 5/8 over the 60 two-qubit stabilizer states and xi(CS) = 8/5 by the Clifford-magic-state theorem of Bravyi, Browne, Calpin, Campbell, Gosset, and Howard, arXiv:1808.00128; an approximate-rank exponent, not a bound on chi) and the T-synthesis exponent 3 log_2(3)/4 = 1.19 from three T gates per CS.
